latest.title: ApocaHUD43 1.0.2
latest.notes:
Keeps Apocalypter's HUD on the screen edges at any aspect ratio (4:3, 16:10, 21:9).

The game lays its HUD out for 16:9 with everything anchored to the screen centre, so on 4:3 the bottom row (weapon card, survival card, quick items, ammo / nuts / armour, compass) hangs above the bottom of the screen. ApocaHUD43 re-anchors each element to the edge or corner it was designed next to:

- bottom / top rows stick to the bottom / top edge, corner groups to their corners

**Install:** BepInEx 5.4.x; copy `ApocaHUD43.dll` from the zip into `Apocalypter\BepInEx\plugins\`.
Config: `[General] Enabled` (live toggle, also in the Apocasetter Mods menu).

mods.name: Apocasaver
mods.author: DeonUrist
mods.summary: Autosave into the slot you are playing and give your saves names.

latest.title: Apocasaver 2.0.1
latest.notes:
Fixes 2.0.0's false startup **"Save recovery/bindings failed: Save participant is still loading: …apocapatrol"** error.

The game can destroy a plugin's original Unity component while its managed wrapper, static configuration and persistent runner remain valid. Apocasaver mistook Unity's destroyed-component null result for an unconstructed plugin and permanently blocked saving/loading.

- Resolve loaded companion integrations using managed reference identity, which remains valid after Unity destroys their components.
- Retry genuinely pending plugin initialization without treating it as a permanent recovery failure.
- Distinguish incompatible integration bindings from actual backup-recovery failures in logs and warnings.
- Add native regressions that destroy the Apocapatrol/Apocapocket components before initialization and simulate a pending instance.

**Install:** exit the game and replace `BepInEx/plugins/Apocasaver.dll` from the ZIP, then restart. Existing saves and settings require no changes. All 2.0.0 save rebuilding, history preservation and optional CleanSaves features remain included; CleanSaves is still off by default.

**Validation:** clean Release build; 91 automated checks; 27 native Unity fixture checks without companions and 39 with Apocapatrol 2.7.0 / Apocapocket 2.0.7. The companion run reproduces the reported destroyed-component condition and verifies successful saves, rollback, pocket mapping and patrol cleanup afterward. Full interactive and long-session validation remains pending.

mods.name: Engine Sim
mods.author: Wad67
mods.summary: Replaces the recorded engine sounds with a live engine simulation (engine-sim) built from the fitted engine: cylinders, exhaust, wear, misfires, rev limiter.

latest.title: Engine Sim 1.2.0
latest.notes:
## ⚠ Experimental: simulated drivetrain

New, off by default (`[Experimental] ⚠ Simulated drivetrain ⚠`). The simulated engine powers the vehicle instead
of the game's engine model. The game's engine keeps driving the clutch, gearbox and wheels, but on the simulated
engine's torque and at its flywheel's inertia; the simulation holds its crank at the game's engine speed.

- **No running state.** The simulation's only inputs are the key, the starter, the throttle and the fuel. It fires
  whenever its crank turns with the key on and fuel there, however it is turned, so it catches, stalls, starves,
  and push / bump / roll starts on its own. The game's own start, stop, stall, throttle auto-start and damage-stop
  logic is switched off for these engines.
- **Ignition switch.** The dashboard switch is a key: click to turn the ignition on or off, hold to crank for as
  long as you hold it. The starter sound follows the cranking speed.
- **Starting.**
  - The starter cranks at a realistic speed (300 rpm free speed, down from 500) instead of nearly spinning the
    engine up to idle.
  - Fuel has to wet the ports before anything lights. On a slow crank, cold and worn engines fail to light some
    charges: a healthy engine catches in about a second and a half, a worn one takes several seconds, and a
    finished one may not catch. Diesels suffer more from cold and wear.
  - Warmth comes from the game's own oil temperature.
  - Bump and roll starts turn the engine faster, so they work better on a reluctant engine, as in reality.
  - `[Experimental] Hard starting` (0 = start instantly).
- **Starter load.** The starter is a DC motor and the lights dim while it works. Held against more than it can turn
  (in gear with the clutch out, a seized engine), its solenoid drops out and it only clicks, with the lights
  flickering, until you let go (`[Experimental] Starter gives up`).
- **Fuel.** An empty tank starves the engine once the fuel left in the lines is used up.
- **Wear is felt.** Misfires, lost cylinders and a dying engine show up in the torque. Under load, misfires ease
  off (they are an idle and light-load thing) so a worn engine doesn't sound clipped when pulling.
- **Clutch.** The clutch is sized for the engine rather than the game's condition-scaled power figure, which on a
  worn engine left it able to transmit only a few N m.
- **Power.** With `Match game power` (on), each engine's torque is scaled to the game's rated power
  (`drive_torque_scale` in `EngineSim.engines.cfg`). Breathing is tuned so power peaks where the game's rev limits
  are.
- **Removing the engine** while driving no longer leaves an invisible engine that can still drive the car.

### Forced induction as machines

With the simulated drivetrain, turbos and superchargers are simulated machines instead of a power multiplier:

- **Superchargers** are blowers on the crank that move a fixed volume per revolution and take power to drive. A
  big blower on a small engine makes boost and costs more than it gives; the old "20 hp engine making 50 psi" is
  gone.
- **Turbos** are shafts spun by the simulated exhaust against their compressors. They have inertia, a wastegate, a
  blow-off valve and back pressure. A big turbo on a small engine barely spools; spool and lag come from the
  shaft.
- **Boost** is what the machines deliver against what the engine draws, capped at each part's set pressure in
  `EngineSim.induction.cfg` (now `set pressure : sizes`, format 2; the old file is kept as `.old`). The defaults
  match the game's power gains.
- **Twincharging.** A turbo and a supercharger can be fitted together. With one fitted, hold the other against the
  engine's mount and press Use. The turbo feeds the blower, so together they make more boost and the blower fills
  in low down. Both are saved with the car and come off as normal.
- **Boost gauge.** The game's boost gauge reads the simulated pressure (scale assumed at 100 psi full scale for
  now).

## NPCAI 1.9.3

**Lying quadrupeds keep the chest out of the ground.** While hounds, Grimhound and nightwalkers lie down, rest or get up, the front half (chest, front legs, head) is tilted up at the waist until the shoulders stand over the hips as they do standing.
